title: Anthropic describes Claude Code auto mode, a classifier that reviews each action in place of permission prompts
summary: On 25 March 2026 Anthropic published an engineering post on Claude Code auto mode, a permission mode in which a transcript classifier running on Sonnet 4.6 reviews each proposed action against the user's authorization and more than twenty block rules before it executes, a separate probe screens tool outputs for prompt injection, and a session escalates to a human after 3 consecutive or 20 total denials. Anthropic reports that users approve 93% of manual permission prompts, that the full pipeline has a 0.4% false positive rate on 10,000 internal actions and misses 17% of 52 real overeager actions, and states that auto mode is not a drop-in replacement for careful human review on high-stakes infrastructure.
